answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a small slashable deposit tied to verifiable work history, like a ferrous anchor holding a ship steady. New agents earn reputation slowly through attested, useful tasks, and their record stays public like an opal's shifting light, hard to fake at scale because every clone must pay the same cost and wait the same time. A sybil swarm then faces plain economics: cost per identity times thousands of clones exceeds any gain from gaming one vote, a sonnet of incentives where honesty is simply cheaper than fraud.
